What's left to do when AI can build everything?

Running it. Someone has to host the agent, watch what it does, fix it when a supplier changes their website, and switch it off when it stops earning its keep.

Most small businesses don't want that job. So at Gee IT we build practical AI agents, then host them and look after them. We run the same agents in our own products every day.

hits.name: GREG ISENBERG
hits.hook: 'Is your business AI proof?' with a points scorecard (0-1 at risk, 2 solid, 3+ really solid). 176 bookmarks.
hits.draft_en:
Is your backup restore-proof?

1 point: it sits with a different provider from the system it protects
1 point: the admin accounts on that system can't delete it
1 point: you've restored from it in the last 90 days
1 point: you know how long that restore took

0-1 = at risk
2 = you'll probably get most of it back
3-4 = solid

Nearly 30 years in disaster recovery taught me to ask these four before anything else. What did you score?
hits.video_tip: 20-30s whiteboard or notepad clip: write the four point lines, tick your own score live, and end on the question 'What did you score?' Pin a reply inviting scores.

hits.draft_en:
Human in the loop might be a liability for code. In property, the human in the loop is the one signing the contract.

Let AI do the boring checks first, like council zoning and the bushfire or flood overlays. Then ring the agent with better questions.

That's why I built FlipPro. Paste an Aussie listing URL and it pulls the property, the suburb, the zoning and every overlay before you've finished scrolling.
hits.video_tip: 20-30s screen recording on flippro.ai: paste a real public listing URL and let the zoning and overlay panel load. Narrate one line per check. Only show screens the FlipPro bot confirms are live.

narrative_synthesis: levelsio carried Sunday again: a question post, 'What's left to do when AI can build everything?', hit 342,069 views, and his 'close your VPS ports' security post hit 249,017 with 3,328 bookmarks. His Claude Code-edited vlog (95,153) set off Greg Isenberg's 'anyone can be a vlogger now' take (56,441). Greg's points scorecard, 'Is your business AI proof?', pulled 176 bookmarks, and Arvid's contrarian 'human-in-the-loop will be a liability' drew 100 replies on 123 likes. The meta is AI doing the work, plus simple scorecards and questions people answer in the replies. Nobody on the watchlist talked about who runs the AI after it's built, whether backups actually restore, or how property buyers check zoning and overlays. Those are Nick's lanes.
